title: Weekend async GPU triage journal
content:
Purpose: quick running log for Saturday/Sunday async triage. Stuff I want to remember, quick commands, and handoff bullets if anyone picks this up. Not polished. Notes-to-self style.

---

Morning scan (first 15 mins)
- check queue latency for p100/p4 pools (esp pool-edge-2) — last night spikes 30-45s for small-gen workloads.
- commands: `kubectl -n gpu-mgt get pods -o wide` then `runnersctl pool status pool-edge-2`
- if queued jobs > 15 for > 10m, look at autoscaler logs (`/var/log/autoscaler/edge-2.log`) and recent scale events in Grafana panel: infra -> autoscale-events.

Quick triage checklist (if I see slowdowns)
- Confirm: Is this capacity pressure or network flakiness?
  - capacity: sustained enqueued tokens + new allocations not provisioning -> consider bumping desired for pool-edge-2 by +2 for warmup.
  - network: packet drops to NVLink bridge or flapping NICs — check `ethtool` counters on host and dmesg for drivers (nvidia-bridge).
- Short-term mitigation: migrate low-priority batch jobs to preemptible pool (pool-batch-ptx). Use label selector: `kubectl label job app=batch-priority=low --overwrite` then requeue.
- Longer: schedule maintenance for suspect racked hosts (rack-r12b) if GPU ECC errors > threshold.

Commands I keep forgetting
- drain node but keep pods for debugging: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl rollout pause ds/gpu-sidecar` (use only if kernel oops suspected)
- clear orphaned MIG slices: `nvidia-smi mig -C` then `nvidia-smi mig -r` (double-check impact, notify Maya first)
- check KV cache hit-ratio (serving runtime): curl internal `/metrics/cache/kv_hit_rate` (prom) or see `serving/runtime/cache` panel

Notes from last incident (ENGOPS-4231)
- root cause: NVLink firmware mismatch across a rack after OS kernel update; some hosts reverted to fallback PCIe path causing ~3x latency on KV refill.
- mitigation we used: roll firmware to v3.1.2 on affected hosts; temporarily rerouted low-latency traffic to pool-dedicated-a while patch rollout completed.
- follow-up: add firmware check to preflight script in release-engineering (ticketed in PR #872).

Things to try this weekend (experiments)
- small canary: enable continuous-batching override on pool-edge-2 for 1h window (10:00-11:00) and measure p50/p95 for small-gen (<=128 tokens).
  - hypothesis: small continuous batches reduce mode-switch overhead and drop p95 by ~10-15%.
  - metrics to capture: token/second, p95 latency, cost-per-1k-tokens.
- experiment: toggle KV prefix caching on route `/v1/stream` for a single deploy tag `canary/kv-2026-03-12` and watch error budgets.

Personal TODOs (urgent)
- [ ] Draft short runbook for weekend on-call with kernel-update checklist (include NVLink firmware verification step). Target: Monday EOD.
- [ ] Add autoscaler backoff tweak to pool config: increase scale-up window from 30s -> 45s to avoid thrash when tail jobs appear. (note: impacts warm latency)
- [ ] Ping Release Eng about adding `nvidia-drivers` pinned version to image builds.

Handover bullets (if I step away)
- If queues > 25 and avg wait > 60s: escalate to SRE channel `#sre-oncall` and paste recent autoscaler logs (last 1h).
- If ECC errors appear on a host: set host to `maintenance` in inventory and open a quick ticket with HW team (include `serial` number from host metadata).
- Contact: Maya Singh (oncall primary), Rafael Ortiz (infra eng), SRE rotation.

Random notes / unresolved questions
- Why did pool-edge-1 show higher KV miss rate at 03:30? Correlate with redis failover? Check `redis-primary` failover logs.
- Consider adding a simple healthcheck endpoint that returns current model serving kernel version and firmware hashes for auditability. Could be lightweight and useful for post-mortems.

Small personal mental-load reminders
- Keep canary windows short (<= 1h) on weekends. Document state before toggling flags.
- If making any config change, add a one-line change note to internal release notes with a rollback step.

End-of-shift quick snapshot (fill before leaving)
- time: ______
- observed queue p95: ____
- any escalations made: Y/N (notes)
- handoff message posted to #gpu-ops: Y/N (link)

---

Tiny checklist for follow-ups next week
- formalize firmware pinning in release pipeline (owner: release-eng)
- add autoscaler hysteresis test to perf-suite
- prototype healthcheck endpoint (owner: me)

Footer
- saved drafts for the canary config in `infra/ops/canaries/weekend-2026-03-12.md` (local repo note).
- keep this doc short and delete or archive after Monday retrospective.

Notes to self: breathe. Don't flip multiple knobs at once on Friday night.
